reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Routes authenticated Google Search Console work through a Composio MCP adapter for site discovery, search analytics, URL indexing inspection, sitemap listing, and sitemap submission using freshly discovered schemas.
neutralIntentExamples: retrieve daily clicks and impressions for an owned property
inspect an authorized page's indexing state before deciding whether to resubmit its sitemap
inputs: authorized property, date range, dimensions, filters, pagination, URL or sitemap, active OAuth connection, and current tool schema
consent for mutations, output destination, data-retention policy, rate budget, and property ownership evidence
operations: discover the current adapter schema and confirm the active connection before selecting a Search Console operation
normalize domain and URL-prefix property identity before paginated analytics or inspection reads
separate read-only reporting from explicit sitemap submission and record request parameters plus returned state
failureBehavior: documents format, freshness, row, sorting, ownership, and sitemap-access pitfalls
depends on live schemas and credentials while omitting consent, audit, retry, and data-export boundaries
exclusions: does not connect an account without user action
does not submit a sitemap from a reporting request
does not treat delayed or top-row analytics as a complete dataset
usefulInvariants: property identity matches the inspected URL
pagination and freshness are explicit
mutating and read-only operations remain separate
materialRisks: analytics may expose commercially sensitive queries
sitemap submission changes external indexing state

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Discovers and executes SharePoint site, library, list, and content operations through a Composio MCP connection, with schema lookup, prerequisite reads, pagination, batching, and connection recovery.
neutralIntentExamples: enumerate an authorized document library through all result pages
update an existing list item only after resolving it and confirming the current tool contract
inputs: authorized tenant scope, resource identity, intended read or mutation, current schema, active connection, page token, and rate limits
document classification, versioning, check-out state, retention, sharing policy, conflict handling, and mutation approval
operations: search the adapter registry for the precise SharePoint capability and materialize any referenced schema
resolve existing sites, lists, libraries, and items before constructing a schema-valid request
execute bounded batches with per-item results, backoff, conflict detection, and an external-write receipt
outputs: SharePoint read result or mutation receipt
pagination, connection, and per-item error evidence
failureBehavior: requires schema discovery, active connection checks, pagination, and response inspection
suggests remote parallel bulk execution without a blast-radius, concurrency, rollback, or content-governance contract
exclusions: does not create a duplicate resource when a match exists
does not run remote bulk loops without bounded authority
does not bypass tenant retention or sharing policy
usefulInvariants: resource identity is resolved before mutation
every page token is accounted for
each external write has an item-level outcome
materialRisks: bulk writes can alter many documents
tool slugs and schemas are mutable

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Investigates technical failures by reproducing them, tracing evidence across boundaries, comparing working patterns, testing one causal hypothesis at a time, adding a failing test, and implementing one verified root-cause fix.
neutralIntentExamples: trace a malformed value backward through a service boundary
distinguish an environmental timeout from an application defect before adding retry behavior
inputs: observed failure, exact errors, reproduction steps, recent changes, component boundaries, working reference, and test surface
authority for instrumentation or changes, sensitive-log policy, rollback, acceptance criteria, and architectural constraints
operations: reproduce the defect and locate the first boundary where observed state diverges from expected state
state one falsifiable causal hypothesis and test it with the smallest non-production probe
encode the reproduction, implement one source-level correction, and rerun focused plus regression verification
failureBehavior: halts guessing, resets after a failed hypothesis, and escalates repeated failures to architectural review
example diagnostics can leak environment data unless redaction and authorization are added
exclusions: does not apply speculative fixes
does not log secrets or unrestricted environments
does not bundle unrelated refactoring with a repair
usefulInvariants: a fix follows causal evidence
one hypothesis changes at a time
completion requires the reproduction and regression suite to pass
materialRisks: overly rigid sequencing can delay urgent containment
a flaky reproduction can support false causality

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Implements JavaScript inside n8n Code nodes using item-mode selection, workflow data accessors, normalized item envelopes, guarded transformations, aggregation, date and query helpers, optional HTTP requests, and workflow-oriented error handling.
neutralIntentExamples: aggregate all incoming workflow items into one typed summary
transform webhook body fields into consistently wrapped n8n output items
inputs: n8n version, Code node mode, incoming item schema, upstream node identities, desired transformation, error policy, and output schema
external-request authority, credentials, item volume, time and memory limits, PII policy, and test fixtures
operations: select all-items or per-item execution from cross-record dependencies and failure semantics
validate input shape and transform values into an array of json-wrapped n8n items on every return path
exercise empty, malformed, webhook, high-volume, helper, and downstream-consumer cases before enabling the node
outputs: input, error, and performance test evidence
failureBehavior: catalogs common access, wrapper, null, expression, and return errors
examples expose raw error messages and tokens and make mutable claims about n8n internals without version gates
exclusions: does not use code for a declarative node that already suffices
does not print confidential item payloads
does not issue HTTP requests without separate external authority
usefulInvariants: all branches return valid item arrays
execution mode matches data dependency
webhook extraction follows the actual fixture shape
materialRisks: helper and data-access APIs can drift

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Uses a Composio MCP adapter to discover DocuSign templates, map recipient roles, create draft envelopes, send them, inspect recipient progress, and add templates while observing one-way lifecycle states.
neutralIntentExamples: prepare a draft envelope from a reviewed template and recipient map
read the recipient-level status of an already authorized envelope
inputs: authorized account, current schema, template and envelope identity, role definitions, recipient names and addresses, message, desired draft or send state, and connection
document authority, recipient consent, legal review, identity verification, retention, delivery timing, and explicit send approval
operations: resolve template identity and exact case-sensitive roles before constructing a recipient map
create an inspectable draft and compare documents, fields, recipients, subject, and irreversible transitions
send or void only under explicit external-action authority and preserve the envelope receipt plus recipient-state evidence
failureBehavior: distinguishes draft, sent, delivered, signed, completed, declined, and voided states
does not impose legal review, recipient verification, duplicate-send protection, or mandatory draft approval
exclusions: does not send from an ambiguous request
does not infer recipient consent from an email address
does not mutate a sent envelope as though it were a draft
usefulInvariants: role names match the selected template
send is a separately authorized transition
stored identifiers originate from current account results
materialRisks: sending creates legal and human consequences
recipient PII crosses a third-party adapter
wrong role mapping can expose documents

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Automates LibreOffice Impress creation, template filling, slide manipulation, and ODP, PPTX, or PDF conversion through soffice commands or UNO scripting.
neutralIntentExamples: convert an ODP deck to PDF in an isolated output directory
generate slides from a reviewed template while retaining an editable ODP source
inputs: source deck or template, requested format, content map, output path, LibreOffice version, font environment, and headless or UNO mode
macro policy, overwrite behavior, unsupported-feature inventory, process ownership, rendering baseline, and file authority
operations: copy the source into an isolated workspace and select command-line conversion or UNO mutation from the requested edit scope
apply template content through format-aware APIs rather than blind XML substitution where structure can change
render every output format and compare slide count, text, media, notes, fonts, transitions, and clipping before delivery
outputs: ODP presentation or converted PPTX or PDF
failureBehavior: mentions socket recovery, editable sources, vector graphics, and conversion testing
claims broad PDF and SWF conversion support and demonstrates unsafe package text replacement without validation or overwrite controls
exclusions: does not kill unrelated office processes
does not overwrite the only source copy
does not claim conversion fidelity without rendered comparison
usefulInvariants: source remains recoverable
slide and note counts are reconciled
each delivered format is rendered and inspected
materialRisks: blind XML replacement can corrupt packages

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Frames Terraform or OpenTofu infrastructure work around reusable modules, isolated environments, encrypted and locked state, provider constraints, policy and security checks, reviewed plans, drift evidence, costs, and maintenance strategy.
neutralIntentExamples: design a versioned module interface with isolated state per environment
review a speculative plan for privilege, replacement, cost, and rollback risk
inputs: infrastructure intent, providers, environments, current state, module graph, organization controls, cost bounds, and deployment authority
backend credentials, disaster recovery, provider lock file, import inventory, policy baseline, blast radius, and rollback evidence
operations: inventory live ownership and state boundaries before designing module interfaces or migration moves
produce a version-pinned plan and evaluate replacements, privileges, dependencies, drift, cost, and policy findings
apply only through an approved pipeline with locking, backups, observability, and post-apply reconciliation
outputs: state, policy, drift, cost, and rollback evidence
failureBehavior: emphasizes plan review, protected state, versioning, tests, policy, drift, and recovery
is mostly a capability inventory and offers no concrete safe state-recovery or apply transaction contract
exclusions: does not apply infrastructure from an unreviewed plan
does not expose state or credentials
does not use targeted operations as routine deployment strategy
usefulInvariants: state has one protected owner
provider and module versions are constrained
planned and actual changes reconcile after apply
materialRisks: multi-cloud abstraction can hide critical differences
automated drift correction can overwrite intentional changes

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Designs AWS Lambda systems with API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS, streams, SAM or CDK, least-privilege infrastructure, partial-batch failure, dead-letter paths, idempotency, cold-start and resource measurements, and runaway-invocation controls.
neutralIntentExamples: design an idempotent SQS consumer with partial retries and a dead-letter queue
measure Lambda initialization and memory before selecting a cost-performance tier
inputs: event sources, handler contract, data stores, latency and cost targets, retry semantics, concurrency, IAM, regions, compliance, and deployment method
current AWS quotas and pricing, account authority, threat model, data classification, rollback, alarms, load evidence, and runtime revisions
operations: model event delivery, duplication, ordering, failure, timeout, and recursion before selecting service integrations
encode least-privilege resources, bounded retries, partial failures, dead letters, idempotency, concurrency brakes, and structured correlation
test locally and in an isolated account, then measure cold starts, duration, memory, payloads, cost, alarms, and rollback before deployment
outputs: failure, security, performance, and cost evidence
failureBehavior: covers retries, dead letters, timeouts, memory, payloads, VPCs, event loops, recursion, alarms, and credential checks
contains mutable service limits, prices, runtimes, and configuration claims plus examples with permissive CORS and destructive development removal
exclusions: does not deploy from examples unchanged
does not grant wildcard IAM
does not create self-triggering event loops
does not expose raw internal errors to clients
usefulInvariants: event processing tolerates duplicate delivery
every asynchronous failure has a terminal path
concurrency and cost have circuit breakers
infrastructure is reviewed before external mutation
materialRisks: misconfigured events can create runaway cost
mutable AWS behavior invalidates stale advice

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Uses a Composio MCP connection to enumerate Snowflake databases, schemas, and tables or execute parameterized SQL under selected database, schema, warehouse, role, session, and timeout context.
neutralIntentExamples: list tables in a named schema using a read-only role
execute a bounded parameterized SELECT after confirming warehouse and namespace
inputs: authorized account, statement or discovery filter, database, schema, warehouse, role, bindings, session parameters, timeout, and current schema
query classification, transaction and rollback plan, row and cost limits, data sensitivity, result destination, and explicit DDL or DML authority
operations: resolve account objects through bounded SHOW operations and record the selected execution context
parse and classify every statement as read, DDL, DML, session change, or multi-statement before dispatch
permit only parameterized and scope-bounded execution under the least privileged role with query ID, row count, cost, and mutation receipt
failureBehavior: mentions bindings, case sensitivity, warehouses, limits, pagination, and statement sequencing
presents arbitrary multi-statement DDL and DML through a third-party adapter without approval, transaction, dry-run, result-size, or cost gates
exclusions: does not execute arbitrary SQL from descriptive intent
does not combine read and mutation statements invisibly
does not select a privileged role by convenience
usefulInvariants: execution context is explicit
user values use bindings
mutations require a distinct authority path
query receipts retain provider identifiers
materialRisks: SQL can destroy or expose warehouse data

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Generates CI definitions that install Newman, run Postman collections with environment and secret injection, fail on test errors, publish JUnit results, and retain HTML reports across major CI platforms.
neutralIntentExamples: add Postman regression tests to a GitHub Actions pull-request gate
publish Newman JUnit evidence from a GitLab pipeline even when assertions fail
inputs: CI platform, collection and environment source, Node and Newman versions, trigger, secret names, reporters, failure policy, and artifact retention
collection trust, target API authority, network policy, package integrity, rate limits, destructive-request controls, and current action versions
operations: inspect the collection for target hosts, mutations, credentials, scripts, and data dependencies before generating a pipeline
pin the runtime, Newman, reporters, and third-party CI actions while mapping secrets through platform-native protected variables
run against an authorized environment and publish redacted JUnit plus HTML artifacts under an always-run evidence step
failureBehavior: preserves reports after test failure and avoids hardcoded credentials
uses global unpinned packages, mutable third-party actions, Node 18 defaults, and does not inspect collections for destructive requests or secret-bearing reports
exclusions: does not run collections against production by default
does not embed secrets in environment files or reports
does not install mutable dependencies without a lock or explicit acceptance
usefulInvariants: assertion failure fails the test job
artifacts publish on both success and failure
secrets remain in protected CI variables
target environment is explicit
materialRisks: reports can leak tokens or response data
CI triggers can create load or cost
